denied_tools.description: Tools blocked for this agent even when the allowlist would admit them. (restart required)

description.description: One line shown in the spawn tool schema so a caller knows when to pick this agent. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning-effort override for this agent. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

execution.description: Where this agent runs. Null inherits the primary lane; host contradicts a configured container profile and is refused. (restart required)

max_response_bytes.description: Ceiling on what this agent returns to its caller, in bytes. Defaults to 5 MiB. (restart required)

model.description: Model override for this agent. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

output_schema.description: Inline JSON Schema the agent answer must conform to: a closed subset of type, properties, required, items, enum and additionalProperties, with every object level forced closed. A non-conforming answer fails the turn instead of being repaired or truncated; an unsupported keyword is refused at load. (restart required)

prompt.description: System prompt used for this agent turns. Empty leaves the agent unguided. (restart required)

provider.description: Harness driving this agent. Null inherits the primary lane setting; blank is refused. (restart required)

security_profile.description: Container posture: workspace can write the checkout, restricted cannot. It never selects host or container placement. (restart required)

tools.description: Tools this agent may call. Empty enforces no allowlist at all, which is warned about at load. (restart required)

agents.description: Logical agents keyed by the id the session tools address them with. The built-in search agent is defined here too. (restart required)

disallowed_tools.description: Tool names withheld from primary-lane turns. Empty withholds nothing beyond the harness defaults. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort handed verbatim to the harness. Null leaves its own default. (restart required)

execution.description: Where primary-lane turns run. Selecting container demands container isolation be on — host is never substituted silently. (restart required)

max_message_chars.description: Characters of one replayed message kept when history is rebuilt. Values under 500 are refused. (restart required)

max_total_chars.description: Characters of replayed history in total. Values under 5000, or below the per-message cap, are refused. (restart required)

max_turns.description: Ceiling on assistant turns inside one exchange. Null leaves the harness default. (restart required)

model.description: Model for main chat, cron and heartbeat turns. Accepts provider/model shorthand; null leaves the choice to the harness. (restart required)

provider.description: Harness driving the primary lane: claude, codex, or an ACP agent id. Must not be blank. (restart required)

burst_threshold.description: Alerts inside the cooldown that collapse into one summary instead of separate messages. (reload)

cooldown_seconds.description: Seconds one alert type is suppressed after firing, so a flapping condition does not spam. (reload)

enabled.description: Deliver operational alerts to the configured targets. Off silences delivery, not the log line. (reload)

additionalProperties.description: Recipients this alert type is delivered to. A non-list value is skipped with a warning. (reload)

routes.description: Which targets each alert type reaches, keyed by alert type. While this map is empty every alert type reaches every configured target; once it holds any entry it acts as an allowlist and a type with no entry reaches nothing. (reload)

targets.description: Where alerts are delivered. An empty list silences delivery even while alerting is on. (reload)

channel.description: Channel the alert is sent over, e.g. signal. Required and non-blank, or the target is skipped. (reload)

recipient.description: Address on that channel, e.g. a phone number or space id. Required and non-blank, or the target is skipped. (reload)

cookie_secure.description: Add the Secure attribute to the session cookie. Needed for HTTPS deployments; it breaks sign-in over plain HTTP. (restart required)

trusted_proxies.description: Addresses whose forwarded-for header is believed when resolving a client IP. Empty believes none. (restart required)

base_url.description: Public URL used to build absolute links for pairing, webhooks and notifications. Null falls back to the bound interface and port. (restart required)

channels.description: Channel integrations keyed by channel name. The built-in channels are declared field by field; any other map-valued key is loaded as the definition of a channel registered by a deployer. Read-only: an object-valued field is written wholesale, so a settable container would carry the read-only Google Chat service account and audience claim past their own refusal. The individual channel fields keep their own tiers. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

debounce_window_ms.description: Milliseconds inbound messages from one session are coalesced into a single turn. Default 1000; 0 starts a turn per message. (restart required)

type.description: Which audience claim an inbound signed request must carry: the app URL, or the numeric project number. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

value.description: Expected audience matching the declared form. A request that fails it is rejected before parsing. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

bot_user.description: Chat user resource name of the bot, used to drop its own messages. Null disables self-filtering. (restart required)

dm_access.description: Who may open a one-to-one Google Chat conversation: pairing demands an invite, allowlist checks the listed senders, open accepts anyone, disabled ignores them. (restart required)

dm_allowlist.description: Approved one-to-one Google Chat senders, used while direct access is allowlist-based. (restart required)

enabled.description: Run the Google Chat integration. Off leaves its transport unstarted. (restart required)
Post progress updates while a long turn runs. (restart required)

min_feedback_delay.description: Duration such as 5s a turn must run before the first progress update appears. (restart required)

status_interval.description: Duration such as 30s between progress updates once they start. (restart required)

status_style.description: Wording of progress updates: creative, minimal, or silent. (restart required)

group_access.description: Which Google Chat groups may reach the agent: allowlist checks the listed groups, open accepts any, disabled ignores them. (restart required)

group_allowlist.description: Approved Google Chat groups, used while group access is allowlist-based. Plain IDs or maps carrying an id plus optional name, project, model and effort. (restart required)

max_chunk_size.description: Accepted and discarded — outbound Google Chat chunking is pinned at 4000 characters. A non-positive value is still reported at load. (restart required)

mention_patterns.description: Accepted and discarded — Google Chat recognizes a mention from the platform annotation, not from a regex. (restart required)

oauth_credentials.description: Path to the OAuth client credentials JSON needed by user-auth features such as Workspace Events subscriptions. (restart required)

max_messages_per_pull.description: Messages requested per pull, between 1 and 100. (restart required)

poll_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between pulls. A lower value costs more API requests. (restart required)

project_id.description: GCP project holding the subscription pulled for asynchronous inbound events. (restart required)

subscription.description: Name of the subscription pulled for inbound events. (restart required)

quote_reply.description: How a reply attributes the inbound message: none, a text attribution line, or a native quoted bubble that needs user-level auth. (restart required)

reactions_auth.description: Reactions need user-level OAuth; disabled turns them off entirely. (restart required)

require_mention.description: Only act on Google Chat group messages that name the bot. Off answers every message in the group. (restart required)

response_prefix.description: Accepted and discarded — Google Chat applies no outbound prefix. (restart required)

service_account.description: Service-account JSON, or a path to it, used for the Chat REST API. Read-only: secret material is never editable through the API. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

enabled.description: Maintain Workspace Events subscriptions. Needs user OAuth plus a topic and subscription. (restart required)

event_types.description: Event types subscribed to, shorthand or fully qualified. Each needs a matching OAuth scope. (restart required)

include_resource.description: Ask for the full resource in each notification. Off delivers name-only events, which have a longer subscription lifetime. (restart required)

pubsub_topic.description: Topic the Workspace Events subscription publishes notifications to. (restart required)

typing_indicator.description: How work in progress is shown: a placeholder message, an emoji reaction, or nothing. A YAML boolean is also accepted, true meaning the placeholder message. (restart required)

webhook_path.description: HTTP path the synchronous Chat webhook is mounted at. (restart required)

max_queue_depth.description: Messages held per session key while a turn is running. Default 100; beyond it, the oldest are dropped. (restart required)

base_delay_ms.description: Milliseconds of backoff before the first delivery retry, grown and jittered on later attempts. Default 1000. (restart required)

jitter_factor.description: Fraction of the backoff randomly added to each delivery retry, spreading a burst of failures apart. 0 retries on a fixed schedule; default 0.2. (restart required)

max_attempts.description: Delivery attempts for one outbound message before it is dead-lettered, for channels that set no policy of their own. Default 3. (restart required)

dm_access.description: Who may open a one-to-one Signal conversation: pairing demands an invite, allowlist checks the listed senders, open accepts anyone, disabled ignores them. (restart required)

dm_allowlist.description: Approved one-to-one Signal senders in E.164 form, used while direct access is allowlist-based. (restart required)

enabled.description: Run the Signal integration. Off leaves the signal-cli daemon unstarted. (restart required)

executable.description: Binary name or absolute path of signal-cli. (restart required)

group_access.description: Which Signal groups may reach the agent: allowlist checks the listed groups, open accepts any, disabled ignores them. (restart required)

group_allowlist.description: Approved Signal groups by base64 id, used while group access is allowlist-based. Maps carrying an id plus optional name, project, model and effort are also accepted. (restart required)

host.description: Address the signal-cli daemon listens on. Default 127.0.0.1. (restart required)

max_chunk_size.description: Largest outbound Signal chunk in characters, multipart labels included. A longer reply is split. Default 4000. (restart required)

mention_patterns.description: Extra regexes counted as naming the bot in a Signal group, on top of the built-in detection. (restart required)

phone_number.description: Account number registered with signal-cli, in E.164 form such as +1234567890. (restart required)

port.description: Port the signal-cli daemon listens on. Default 8080. (restart required)

require_mention.description: Only act on Signal group messages that name the bot. Off answers every message in the group. (restart required)

response_prefix.description: Accepted and discarded — Signal applies no outbound prefix. Registered because the shared channel parser reads the key for every channel, so a config carrying it must still load. (restart required)

dm_access.description: Who may open a one-to-one WhatsApp conversation: pairing demands an invite, allowlist checks the listed senders, open accepts anyone, disabled ignores them. (restart required)

dm_allowlist.description: Approved one-to-one WhatsApp senders, used while direct access is allowlist-based. (restart required)

enabled.description: Run the WhatsApp integration. Off leaves the GOWA sidecar unstarted. (restart required)

gowa_db_uri.description: Connection string giving the GOWA sidecar persistent pairing state. Null keeps its own local store. (restart required)

gowa_executable.description: Binary name or absolute path of the GOWA sidecar that talks to WhatsApp. (restart required)

gowa_host.description: Address the GOWA sidecar HTTP API listens on. Default 127.0.0.1. (restart required)

gowa_port.description: Port the GOWA sidecar HTTP API listens on. Default 3000; an instance already listening there is attached to rather than spawned. (restart required)

group_access.description: Which WhatsApp groups may reach the agent: allowlist checks the listed groups, open accepts any, disabled ignores them. (restart required)

group_allowlist.description: Approved WhatsApp groups, used while group access is allowlist-based. Plain JIDs, or maps carrying an id plus optional name, project, model and effort. (restart required)

max_chunk_size.description: Largest outbound WhatsApp chunk in characters, multipart labels included. A longer reply is split. Default 4000. (restart required)

mention_patterns.description: Extra regexes counted as naming the bot in a WhatsApp group, on top of the built-in detection. (restart required)

require_mention.description: Only act on WhatsApp group messages that name the bot. Off answers every message in the group. (restart required)

response_prefix.description: Template prepended to the first outbound WhatsApp chunk. Understands the {model} and {agent.identity.name} placeholders. (restart required)

max_parallel_turns.description: Ceiling on agent turns executing simultaneously across the instance. Raising it multiplies peak token spend. (reload)

enabled.description: Run agent work inside container isolation. Left unset, DartClaw isolates wherever a container runtime is detected and starts in advisory mode where none is; an explicit true instead fails startup when the host cannot isolate. POSIX only; off means guards are the whole boundary. Read-only: placement is a deterministic keep, and clearing it through the API would either strand an explicit container selection at the next boot or move neutral-profile work onto the host. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

image.description: Container image agent work is executed in. Default dartclaw-agent:latest. (restart required)

compact_instructions.description: Extra guidance handed to the model when it compacts a conversation. Null uses the built-in wording. (restart required)

identifier_instructions.description: The custom wording used when identifier preservation is set to custom. (restart required)

identifier_preservation.description: How hard compaction works to keep literal identifiers: strict, off, or custom wording. (restart required)

max_result_bytes.description: Outer cap in bytes on every successful tool result the MCP endpoint returns. An oversized one arrives as head and tail around a truncation marker. (reload)

reserve_tokens.description: Tokens held back from the window so a compaction flush always fits. (reload)

warning_threshold.description: Percentage of the window at which the UI warns about remaining room. Clamped to 50–99. (live)

api_key.description: The key itself, normally an environment reference so the literal stays out of the file. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

repository.description: Optional owner/name scope guard limiting where a GitHub token may be used. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

token.description: The GitHub token, normally an environment reference so the literal stays out of the file. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

type.description: Which kind of secret the entry holds. Omitted means an API key. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

credentials.description: API-key and GitHub-token entries keyed by the name other sections reference. Read-only: secret material is never editable through the API, and subscription credentials never live here. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

data_dir.description: Instance directory holding sessions, the workspace, databases and credential stores. Default ~/.dartclaw. (restart required)

dev_mode.description: Serve assets from the checkout instead of the embedded copies and relax caching. Never leave it on in production. (restart required)

enabled.description: Route messages in a bound thread straight to that task session, and post task notifications as new threads. Google Chat only — it is the one channel that carries a thread identity to bind. (restart required)

idle_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes of thread inactivity before the binding is dropped. The sweep runs every five minutes, so removal can lag. (restart required)

auth_mode.description: token demands the bearer credential on every request; none serves the instance unauthenticated. Read-only through the API — change it in YAML. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

hsts.description: Send Strict-Transport-Security on responses. Safe only once the instance is reached over HTTPS everywhere. (restart required)

mcp_clients.description: Named MCP clients allowed to reach /mcp with their own bearer token, each limited to the context-engine read tools. Read-only through the API, and each token must be a ${VAR} reference. Empty leaves /mcp accepting the gateway token alone. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

name.description: Client name. Appears as the audit principal for every tool call the client makes. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

token.description: Bearer credential written as a ${VAR} environment reference. A literal value, or a reference resolving to nothing, refuses to start. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

debounce_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait after a file change before applying it, so an editor writing twice reloads once. Minimum 100. (restart required)

mode.description: How a YAML edit reaches the running server: off never, signal on SIGHUP, auto on file change. (restart required)

token.description: Bearer credential accepted by the API and web UI. Generated when omitted, and never editable through the API. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

enabled.description: Accept inbound webhook deliveries and map them onto workflow runs. (restart required)

triggers.description: Rules mapping an inbound event onto the workflow that should launch. (restart required)

actions.description: Event actions that launch the workflow, e.g. opened and synchronize. Omitted uses those two. (restart required)

event.description: Webhook event the rule matches. Only pull_request is processed today; omitted defaults to it. (restart required)

labels.description: Labels the pull request must carry. Empty applies no label filter. (restart required)

workflow.description: Name of the workflow definition launched on a match. Omitted defaults to code-review. (restart required)

webhook_path.description: HTTP path the webhook endpoint is mounted at. (restart required)

webhook_secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 key deliveries are signed with. Required once the handler is on; an unsigned delivery is refused. (restart required)

admin_senders.description: Sender IDs exempt from rate limits and budget blocks. (restart required)

action.description: What happens once the allowance is spent: refuse new turns, or only warn. (restart required)

daily_tokens.description: Token allowance per day across the instance. 0 means unlimited. (restart required)

timezone.description: Zone whose midnight resets the allowance. Accepts UTC, UTC±N, and DST-aware IANA names. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort for crowd-coding turns. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

model.description: Model used for crowd-coding turns. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

action.description: What a detected runaway triggers: aborting the turn, or a warning only. (restart required)

enabled.description: Watch for a runaway agent and stop it. Off by default. (restart required)

max_consecutive_identical_tool_calls.description: Repeated identical tool calls tolerated before the action fires. 0 mutes this signal. (restart required)

max_consecutive_turns.description: Consecutive turns tolerated before the action fires. 0 mutes this signal. (restart required)

max_tokens_per_minute.description: Token velocity tolerated before the action fires. 0 mutes this signal. (restart required)

velocity_window_minutes.description: Minutes the velocity average is computed over. (restart required)

queue_strategy.description: How waiting turns are picked: fifo by arrival, or fair round-robin across senders. (restart required)

turns.description: Agent turns allowed inside the window across every sender. 0 lifts the limit. (restart required)

window.description: Length of the instance-wide sliding window in minutes; YAML also accepts shorthand such as 5m or 1h. (restart required)

max_pause_queued.description: Messages held back per sender while a turn is paused. 0 drops them. (restart required)

max_queued.description: Messages held back per sender once the limit is hit; further ones are dropped. 0 drops immediately. (restart required)

messages.description: Messages one sender may send inside the window. 0 lifts the limit. (restart required)

window.description: Length of the sliding window in minutes; YAML also accepts shorthand such as 5m or 1h. (restart required)

stall_action.description: What a stalled turn triggers: a warning, a cancellation, or nothing. (restart required)

stall_timeout.description: Duration such as 300s without provider progress before the stall action fires; zero disables it. (restart required)

turn_timeout.description: Wall-clock ceiling such as 1800s for a provider turn; zero disables it. (restart required)

max_retention_days.description: Days of dated audit partitions kept before deletion. 0 keeps them indefinitely. (restart required)

extra_blocked_patterns.description: Regexes added to the built-in destructive-command set. An invalid pattern fails the guard build rather than being skipped silently.Read-only here: the guard-editor endpoints own writes to this path, and they normalize each entry and refuse a change the guard build rejects. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

extra_blocked_pipe_targets.description: Programs added to the built-in set that must never be piped into, such as an interpreter reading from a download.Read-only here: the guard-editor endpoints own writes to this path, and they normalize each entry and refuse a change the guard build rejects. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

classifier.description: Which classifier runs: the local Claude binary, or the Anthropic API. (restart required)

enabled.description: Classify model-visible content before it reaches the agent. (restart required)

fail_open.description: Let unscorable content through when the classifier itself fails. Turning it on means unchecked material can reach the agent. (restart required)

max_bytes.description: Bytes handed to the classifier; longer material is truncated before scoring. (restart required)

model.description: Model the classifier uses. A cheaper one lowers the cost of every scan. (restart required)

enabled.description: Master switch for the whole guard pipeline. On by default; read-only, because turning enforcement off is a YAML-and-restart decision, not an API call. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

fail_open.description: Whether an unexpected guard failure warns instead of blocking. Fail-closed by default; read-only for the same reason as the master switch. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

extra_rules.description: Path rules added to the built-in protections. Two rules over one pattern with different levels fail the guard build.Read-only here: the guard-editor endpoints own writes to this path, and they normalize each entry and refuse a change the guard build rejects. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

level.description: How far access is cut: no_access blocks everything, read_only blocks writes and deletes, no_delete blocks deletes only. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

pattern.description: Glob the rule applies to, e.g. **/*.secret. Required and non-blank. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

extra_domains.description: Hosts this agent turns may additionally reach. An empty list drops the override entirely. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

agent_overrides.description: Per-logical-agent outbound widenings keyed by agent id. They add to the allowlist and never narrow it.Read-only here: the guard-editor endpoints own writes to this path, and they normalize each entry and refuse a change the guard build rejects. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

extra_allowed_domains.description: Hosts added to the built-in outbound allowlist. Every fetch target an MCP deployment needs must be listed here.Read-only here: the guard-editor endpoints own writes to this path, and they normalize each entry and refuse a change the guard build rejects. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

extra_exfil_patterns.description: Regexes added to the built-in exfiltration detectors. An invalid pattern fails the guard build.Read-only here: the guard-editor endpoints own writes to this path, and they normalize each entry and refuse a change the guard build rejects. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

args.description: Arguments passed to the executable, e.g. the ACP subcommand and its builtins. (restart required)

binary.description: Executable spawned for this ACP client. Required — a registration without it is skipped. (restart required)

container_isolation_required.description: Demands a container, which ACP has no runnable execution for — a true here is refused at startup. (restart required)

container_profile.description: Container posture the execution policy would resolve to. Leaving it set on a container-enabled deployment pins the agent to a refused policy. (restart required)

credential.description: Names a credentials entry whose API key is injected under the environment variable it declares. The only credential an ACP spawn ever carries. (restart required)

model_provider.description: Vendor whose model the client talks to. It selects validation and routing, never a credential. (restart required)

required_builtins.description: Builtins the client must load, e.g. developer for a guarded Goose registration. (restart required)

requires_guard_mediation.description: Operator declaration that the guard chain sees this client tool calls. It demands a direct topology plus evidence. (restart required)

topology.description: How the client reaches its model. Omitted means unverified, which claims no guard mediation. (restart required)

verification.description: Evidence backing a guard-mediation claim, e.g. startup_probe. Required once mediation is claimed. (restart required)

agents.description: ACP provider identities keyed by id. Each registration defines a spawn and its security classification; ACP runs on the host only. (restart required)

host.description: Interface the HTTP server binds. Default localhost — bind 0.0.0.0 only behind a trusted proxy. (restart required)

delivery_mode.description: Where the run report goes: nowhere, announced in chat, or posted to a webhook. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort of the extraction turn. Billed per file — lower it for raw material you genuinely want compressed. (restart required)

enabled.description: Watch the filesystem inbox and ingest what is dropped there. Off by default; every file costs one extraction turn. (restart required)

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between sweeps of the drop directory. Clamped to 1–1440. (restart required)

max_bytes.description: Largest source file that will be read, in bytes. Anything above it is skipped. (restart required)

processed_retention_days.description: Days an already-ingested source is kept before deletion. 0 keeps it indefinitely. (restart required)

retry_attempts.description: How often the nondeterministic extraction turn is retried before the source is quarantined. (restart required)

delivery_mode.description: Where the lint report goes: nowhere, announced in chat, or posted to a webhook. (restart required)

enabled.description: Run the wiki lint report on a schedule. It reports only and never rewrites a page. (restart required)

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between lint runs. Clamped to 1–1440. (restart required)

file.description: Path written in addition to stdout. Null logs to stdout only. (restart required)

format.description: human is readable in a terminal; json emits line-delimited records for a log shipper. (restart required)

level.description: Lowest severity written out. FINE includes per-turn detail and is noisy in production. (restart required)

redact_patterns.description: Regexes whose matches are masked before any line is written out. (reload)

allow_tools.description: Tools this server may actually run. Empty denies every outbound call. (restart required)

command.description: Executable launched for a stdio server. Exactly one of it and url must be present. (restart required)

credential.description: Names a credentials entry presented to this server. Without one the server is disabled — never inline a secret here. (restart required)

enabled.description: Whether the server is used. It is forced off at load when its credential does not resolve. (restart required)

network_class.description: How far the server can reach, which decides what egress mediation applies. Required. (restart required)

calls.description: Calls permitted inside the window. 0 leaves the server unthrottled. (restart required)

window_seconds.description: Length of the call window in seconds. Defaults to 60. (restart required)

surface_tools.description: Tools listed to the harness. Empty exposes none, so the model never sees them. (restart required)

tokens.description: Tokens this server results may consume inside the window. 0 leaves it unbudgeted. (restart required)

window_seconds.description: Length of the token window in seconds. Defaults to 60. (restart required)

url.description: Absolute endpoint of an HTTP server. Plain http is accepted only for a literal loopback host. (restart required)

mcp_servers.description: External MCP servers keyed by the name their tools are surfaced under. Each entry declares exactly one transport. (restart required)

enabled.description: Revise, merge and remove canonical memory entries on a schedule. Opt-in, and it costs one turn per run. (restart required)

schedule.description: Cron expression driving the curation run. (restart required)

enabled.description: Distil each day of turn logs into canonical observations. Opt-in, and it costs one turn per run. (restart required)

schedule.description: Cron expression driving the distillation run. (restart required)

max_bytes.description: Byte budget applied to each prompt memory projection – the index and the errors section – independently. Must be positive; a larger budget spends more of every prompt. (restart required)

archive_after_days.description: Days before a canonical memory entry is archived. Must be positive. (restart required)

enabled.description: Archive and de-duplicate recognized memory entries on a schedule. Unrecognized content is preserved either way. (restart required)

schedule.description: Cron expression driving the archival run. (restart required)

name.description: Display label for this instance, shown in the web UI and in channel replies. (restart required)

expiry_days.description: Days a pairing invitation stays valid. Minimum 1; an expired invite must be re-issued. (restart required)

port.description: TCP port the HTTP server binds. Default 3333; excluded from hot reload, so a change needs a restart. (restart required)

branch.description: Ref tracked and branched from. Defaults to main for a remote, and to the current checkout branch for a local path. (restart required)

strategy.description: How much history is fetched. shallow is cheapest; full is needed for history-dependent work. (restart required)

credentials.description: Names a github-token credentials entry used for pushes and pull requests. (restart required)

default.description: Pick this project when a new task names none. (restart required)

localPath.description: Existing checkout used directly. Must be absolute, free of traversal, and inside the allowlist. (restart required)

draft.description: Open the pull request as a draft so review is opt-in. (restart required)

labels.description: Labels applied to every pull request this project opens. (restart required)

strategy.description: What a finished task produces: a pushed branch only, or a GitHub pull request. (restart required)

remote.description: Git URL cloned for this project. Exactly one of it and localPath must be supplied. (restart required)

projects.description: Absolute directories a local-path project may live under. Empty bounds nothing, which is why it gates the API flag. Read-only for the same reason: widening it through the API would lift its own bound. (restart required)

allowApiLocalPath.description: Let the API register projects pointing at existing host directories. Downgraded to false unless an allowlist bounds it. Read-only: it decides whether the API may reach the host filesystem, so it must not itself be settable through the API. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

fetchCooldownMinutes.description: Minutes a freshness check skips the git fetch after a successful one. Default 5. (restart required)

localPathAllowlist.description: Absolute directories a local-path project may live under. Empty bounds nothing, which is why it gates the API flag. Read-only for the same reason: widening it through the API would lift its own bound. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

approval.description: Prompt-gating axis. Only never opts a trusted run into full access. (restart required)

auth.description: Which credential is presented. Unset lets an alias inherit its family choice; a forced value never falls back to the other kind. (restart required)

executable.description: Binary name or path launched for this provider. Required — an entry without it is skipped at load. (restart required)

inherit_user_settings.description: Claude only. True loads user, project and local settings; false passes project-only sources. (restart required)

pool_size.description: Hard ceiling on concurrent worker leases for this provider. 0 means the default of one. (restart required)

sandbox.description: OS-isolation axis: read-only, workspace-write or danger-full-access. A map value is forwarded verbatim as a raw native settings block. (restart required)

providers.description: Harness providers keyed by id. Keys beyond the ones declared here are forwarded verbatim as provider-specific options. (restart required)

enabled.description: Run the periodic unattended turn. Off means nothing fires from the schedule. (live)

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between heartbeat turns. Each one costs a full turn of tokens. (restart required)

jobs.description: Unattended jobs, each firing a prompt turn or creating a task. Their prompt bodies are never validated here — an empty one only fails when the job runs. (restart required)

delivery.description: Where the result goes: nowhere, announced in chat, or posted to a webhook. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning-effort override for this job turn. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

enabled.description: Whether the job is active. Defaults to true. (restart required)

id.description: Stable identifier for this job. Required; name is accepted as a compatibility alias. (restart required)

model.description: Model override for this job turn. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

name.description: Compatibility alias for id. Prefer id in new configs. (restart required)

prompt.description: Text handed to the agent when a prompt job fires. Required for that kind, and passed through unvalidated. (restart required)

attempts.description: How often a failed firing is retried. Defaults to 0, meaning no retry. (restart required)

delay_seconds.description: Seconds waited between retries. Defaults to 60. (restart required)

schedule.description: Shorthand form: a bare five-field cron expression, equivalent to a cron map with that expression. (restart required)

at.description: ISO-8601 instant a once schedule fires at. Required for that kind, and an unparseable value is refused. (restart required)

expression.description: Five-field cron expression. Required for a cron schedule, and a job without one is refused. (restart required)

minutes.description: Minutes between firings for an interval schedule. Must be at least 1, or the job is refused. (restart required)

type.description: Map form: which schedule kind the entry carries. Omitted inside a map means cron. (restart required)

task.description: Template the created task is built from. Required when the kind is task. (restart required)

acceptance_criteria.description: What the created task must satisfy before it is considered finished. (restart required)

auto_start.description: Queue the created task at once instead of leaving it a draft. Defaults to true. (restart required)

description.description: Body handed to the agent as the task brief. Required. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning-effort override for the created task. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

model.description: Model override for the created task. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

task_type.description: Retired compatibility alias. Optional and ignored; research and coding are refused. (restart required)

title.description: Title given to the created task. Required. (restart required)

token_budget.description: Token ceiling for the created task. Null leaves it unbudgeted. (restart required)

type.description: Retired compatibility field. Optional and ignored; research and coding are refused. (restart required)
What firing does: run a prompt turn, or create a task from the block below. Defaults to prompt. (restart required)

webhook_url.description: Endpoint the result is posted to when delivery is by webhook. (restart required)

backend.description: Engine behind memory search: fts5 uses the bundled SQLite index, qmd delegates to a local daemon. (restart required)

default_depth.description: Effort a query spends when the caller names none: fast, standard or deep. (restart required)

api_key.description: Vendor API key, normally an environment reference such as ${BRAVE_API_KEY}. Exactly one of it and credential is required — an entry with neither, or both, is skipped. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

credential.description: Name of a credentials.<name> api-key entry to authenticate with, from the config file or the named credential store. Exactly one of it and api_key is required; an unknown name, a github-token entry or a blank value skips the provider. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

enabled.description: Whether this vendor may be queried. Required — an entry without it is skipped at load. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

providers.description: Web-search vendors keyed by provider id; brave and tavily are the recognized ids. Read-only: each entry carries or names a credential, which is never editable through the API. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

host.description: Loopback address of the qmd daemon. Only localhost, 127.x.x.x and ::1 are accepted. (restart required)

port.description: TCP port the qmd daemon listens on. Default 8181. (restart required)

env_allowlist.description: Environment variable names a workflow bash step may read, added to the built-in set. Everything else is stripped from its environment. (restart required)

extra_strip_patterns.description: Extra regexes whose matches are removed from bash-step output before the model sees it. (restart required)

dm_scope.description: Overrides how this channel one-to-one messages map onto sessions. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning-effort override for turns arriving on this channel. (restart required)

group_scope.description: Overrides how this channel group messages map onto sessions. (restart required)

model.description: Model override for turns arriving on this channel. (restart required)

channels.description: Per-channel overrides keyed by channel name. An entry that sets nothing is dropped rather than stored empty. (restart required)

dm_scope.description: How direct messages map onto sessions: one shared, one per contact, or one per contact per channel. (live)

effort.description: Reasoning effort for scoped conversational turns. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

group_scope.description: How group messages map onto sessions: one shared per group, or one per member. (live)

idle_timeout_minutes.description: Minutes of silence before an eligible session resets. 0 turns the timeout off. (reload)

cron_retention_hours.description: Hours an orphaned cron session survives before deletion. 0 deletes none. (restart required)

max_disk_mb.description: Disk budget in megabytes for stored sessions. 0 means unbudgeted. (restart required)

max_sessions.description: Cap on retained sessions, oldest pruned first. 0 means uncapped. (restart required)

mode.description: warn reports what maintenance would remove; enforce removes it. (restart required)

prune_after_days.description: Days of inactivity after which a session is archived. 0 archives nothing. (restart required)

schedule.description: Cron expression driving the automatic maintenance run. An empty string disables it. (restart required)

model.description: Model used for scoped conversational turns. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

reset_hour.description: Local hour at which main, channel and cron sessions are archived and restarted under the same key. -1 keeps them until idle timeout or maintenance. User-created sessions are never reset. (reload)

source_dir.description: Checkout root used to locate templates and static assets during development. Null uses the embedded copies. (restart required)

static_dir.description: Directory served at /static. Null resolves under the checkout root, then the embedded copies. (restart required)

artifact_retention_days.description: Days a finished task keeps its artifacts before maintenance deletes them. 0 keeps them indefinitely. (restart required)

default_max_tokens.description: Token ceiling applied to a task that names none. Any value at or below zero means unbudgeted, which is also the default. (restart required)

warning_threshold.description: Fraction of a task token budget at which it warns once, between 0 and 1. Defaults to 0.8; the task still fails at the full budget regardless. (restart required)

completion_action.description: What a finished task does next: review parks it for a human, accept lands it without one. (restart required)

execution.description: Execution mode for background tasks. container demands container isolation be on; task security profiles are declared separately through the authenticated task API. (file-only, not settable via API or CLI)

base_ref.description: Git ref a task worktree branches from. (restart required)

merge_strategy.description: How an accepted task lands: squash collapses its commits into one, merge keeps them. (restart required)

stale_timeout_hours.description: Hours an idle task worktree survives before cleanup removes it. (restart required)

templates_dir.description: Directory the Trellis page templates load from. Null resolves under the checkout root, then the embedded copies. (restart required)

budget_warning_tokens.description: Daily token count that raises a warning banner. Null shows no warning. (restart required)

max_file_size_bytes.description: Largest upload accepted through the web UI and channels, in bytes. (restart required)

approvals.description: How far a run advances unattended: manual pauses on stalls and approval steps, auto-on-stall passes stalls only, auto passes both. (restart required)

delete_remote_branch_on_failure.description: Delete the pushed branch when a run fails. Off keeps it for post-mortem inspection. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort for executor-role steps. Null inherits the workflow-role setting. (restart required)

model.description: Model for executor-role steps. Accepts provider/model shorthand. (restart required)

provider.description: Harness driving executor-role steps. Null inherits the workflow-role setting. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort for planner-role steps. Null inherits the workflow-role setting. (restart required)

model.description: Model for planner-role steps. Accepts provider/model shorthand. (restart required)

provider.description: Harness driving planner-role steps. Null inherits the workflow-role setting. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort for reviewer-role steps. Null inherits the workflow-role setting. (restart required)

model.description: Model for reviewer-role steps. Accepts provider/model shorthand. (restart required)

provider.description: Harness driving reviewer-role steps. Null inherits the workflow-role setting. (restart required)

effort.description: Reasoning effort for workflow-level steps when a step names none. Null leaves the harness default. (restart required)

model.description: Model for workflow-level turns when a step names none. Accepts provider/model shorthand. (restart required)

provider.description: Harness driving workflow-level turns when a step names none. Null inherits the primary lane setting. (restart required)

mode.description: Whether stale run artifacts are only reported (warn) or actually deleted (enforce) during maintenance. (restart required)

prune_after_days.description: Age in days past which run artifacts are pruned. 0 keeps them indefinitely. (restart required)

workspace_dir.description: Operator-owned checkout the workflow steps run in. Null lets DartClaw manage one under the instance directory and refresh its AGENTS.md on upgrade. (restart required)

enabled.description: Commit workspace changes to the local repository on the git-sync schedule. Off by default. (live)

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between workspace git-sync runs. The job owns this schedule; it no longer rides the heartbeat cycle. (restart required)

push_enabled.description: Also push those commits to the configured remote. Ignored while git sync itself is off. (live)
